--------
Rex Holloway sits down with Vlad to explain how tensions between the Aryan Brotherhood of Texas (ABT) and the Aryan Circle escalated into a violent prison conflict in the late 1990s. Holloway traces the feud to Texas facilities including the Terrell Unit, now Polunsky Unit in Livingston, McConnell Unit, Ferguson Unit, and Eastham, describing how rumors, stabbings, chain-bus attacks, and shifting gang alliances fueled the war.

He also discusses prison “grapevine” politics, administrative segregation, confirmed gang status, and why younger, more aggressive recruits helped intensify violence behind bars. Holloway reflects on the complicated reality of knowing men on both sides, including former Aryan Circle members who joined ABT, and the brutal expectations that came with switching affiliations.

A raw look at Texas prison gangs, true crime history, and the deadly logic of institutional gang warfare.

--------
In this VladTV interview, former Mexican Mafia member Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza reflects on his 1975 arrest in Kern County tied to the Bakersfield killings of the Reyes brothers, the looming death penalty, and how California’s 1976 ruling changed his fate to a potential life sentence. Speaking with DJ Vlad, Mendoza explains the gang’s code around dropouts, informants, and why “ratting” carried a deadly consequence inside La Eme. He discusses his standing in the organization, the violent reputation that earned trust among members, and names influential figures like Joe Morgan and Kilroy. Mendoza also describes the mindset behind gang loyalty, prison culture, court strategy, and his later undercover cooperation against the Mexican Mafia. The conversation includes comparisons to Brian “Glaze” Gibbs and the Queens crack era, offering a stark look at organized crime, conscience, and survival in California’s prison underworld.

Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee sits down with Vlad to react to Keefe D’s post-verdict interview, where he dismissed the alleged Diddy $1 million hit story as a “script” pushed by lawyers and writer Chuck Phillips—and suggested lawsuits could make him a multimillionaire. Dirt Rocc questions how a “scripted” story could stay consistent across multiple interviews, while also weighing the reality of a guilty verdict in a murder case, the reported 10-to-25-year plea offer, and the possibility of a life sentence at age 63. The conversation also covers courtroom behavior, sentencing strategy, remorse, and why focusing on seized property or future lawsuits may not help with the judge ahead of sentencing. A candid discussion on Keefe D, the Tupac Shakur case, Diddy allegations, legal consequences, and the high-stakes choices defendants face.
